title: Would you actually use AI for the boring parts of trading?
author: Warm_Date7306
selftext: I'm less interested in an AI tool telling me where to enter a trade and more interested in the things that are easy to calculate or look up incorrectly. An AI assistant that handles things like position sizing, drawdown calculations, payout estimates, market charts and explanations of platform rules seems more useful to me than one trying to make the trading decisions. What would you actually want an AI assistant to handle while you keep the trading decisions yourself?

comments.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
comments.body: I am in the process of building out a fully automated system with the help of AI. I will let you know in a couple of months lol.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
yes, and the first boring job I'd hand over is reconciliation, which never makes these lists. did the fill match the order, does the position at the broker match the position in my notes, did the stop actually get placed. sizing is arithmetic, I can do arithmetic. checking a hundred small things at 16:05 every day is where I get sloppy, and an assistant that only reports mismatches earns its keep there. the moment it starts suggesting entries I stop trusting the rest of it.

my own paper desk grew out of that exact split, Quantradin, mine, I built it, find it at quantradin.com: it does the bookkeeping and the grading and never picks an entry.
